scenes.narration: Three moves and Qwen Image two point one edits your photos tonight. The folder you keep meaning to fix stays on your own drive.

Qwen Image two point one is a single model. It makes pictures, and it edits the ones you already have. You hand it a photo and an instruction, like change the background to a sunset beach. Everything outside the edit stays put. People still look like themselves.

Here's the wall. The part that paints the image, the transformer, is fourteen point two three gigabytes at full precision. The text encoder, the part that reads your instruction, is even bigger. That does not fit a gaming card.

Quantization is the shrink: each stored weight keeps fewer bits. Think of pi with its long tail rounded off. The number still works, and the file gets much smaller. You trade a little fidelity, and the loss is not even; exact math notices first. Unsloth ships the shrink as an int eight file, seven point two six gigabytes on disk.

Unsloth says its F P eight build, another eight-bit format, runs in six gigabytes of video memory, using offloading. Offloading parks pieces of the model in system memory and swaps them in as needed. Treat those figures as Unsloth's estimates, not tested minimums. Slower, yes, but gentler than you would guess. Your patience does the heavy lifting.
Step one: install Unsloth Desktop on your gaming PC. It is the app that runs these models locally. Let it update to the latest version.
Step two: pick Qwen Image two point one in the Model hub and choose int eight. It is the safer pick for fidelity. The app downloads the quant and uses it automatically.

Step three: open the Edit tab, load your photo, and type your edit: remove the watch. Hit generate, and lower the resolution if memory runs out. The watch is gone, and everything else is exactly where you left it.
